title: Cao Cao Rallies the Lords; Three Heroes Fight Lü Bu at Hulao Pass
summary: Cao Cao's forged summons brings the lords out with their armies — seventeen contingents, each complete with its own officers, camped in a line two hundred li long. They elect Yuan Shao their chief on a three-storeyed altar, smear the blood of the sacrifice on their lips, and immediately begin to quarrel about supplies.

At Sishui Pass Dong Zhuo's champion Hua Xiong kills every man sent against him. A nameless bowman in Gongsun Zan's train asks to try; Cao Cao pours him wine to send him off; he returns with the head and the wine is still warm.
At Hulao Pass Lü Bu breaks every commander in turn until all three brothers ride at him at once, and even then he only withdraws.
history: The coalition existed and achieved almost nothing. Guan Yu never met Hua Xiong, who was killed by Sun Jian's troops, and the three-on-one at Hulao is pure novel — the most famous fight in the book has no history behind it at all. The novel also loses the real shape of the alliance: it musters the lords in one unnamed line of camps, where in fact they sat in three separate groups — the largest at Suanzao, Yuan Shao at Henei, Yuan Shu at Nanyang — which is why they never combined.

pins.note: Forged the summons that raised it.
Driven off the pass by stones, starved of grain by Yuan Shu, and burnt out at midnight.
Arrives in Gongsun Zan's train, unranked.
Kills Hua Xiong before the wine cools.
Holds the pass until Guan Yu.
Fights all three brothers at once.
In charge of supply, and withholds it from Sun Jian.
Wears his lord's purple turban to draw the pursuit, and dies wearing it.
Kills Hu Zhen with a thrust through the throat.
Sent with Guo Si to exterminate Yuan Wei's household, then to hold Sishui.
Spends his fortune to raise the volunteer corps.
Arrives with his brother and a company each.
